exposure: lunar phases (full moon, new moon, other lunar phases)
outcome: adverse neonatal short-term health (pH of < 7.2 and/or a 5-min Apgar score of < 7)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 462,947 singleton births delivered at >= 23+0 gestational weeks with a birthweight of >= 500g, excluding women who underwent elective cesarean or labor induction.
finding: The study found no significant influence of different moon phases on standardized birth ratio or adverse neonatal outcomes, but observed a trend towards prolonged maximum duration of labor during nighttime births related to moon phases.
